text:
### Observed differences

- Two five-activity blocks swapped their roles. In the earlier window, A16, A17, A18, A19 and A20 each ran in about 85 in 100 traces; in the later window, only about 18 in 100. A21, A22, A23, A24 and A25 show the mirror image: about 16 in 100 traces earlier, about 82 in 100 later. None of the ten activities repeats within a trace in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- The routing out of A15 flipped accordingly: earlier, about 85 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions led to A19 and about 15 to A24; in the later window, about 82 led to A24 and about 18 to A19. [DIR001]
- A15's company changed: earlier it was followed by each of A16–A20 in about 85 in 100 traces and ran without A21–A25 in about 85 in 100; in the later window it runs without A16–A20 in about 82 in 100 traces and precedes A21–A25 in about 82 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- Block cohesion swapped: pairs within A16–A20 co-occurred in about 85 in 100 traces earlier versus about 18 later (in about 82 in 100 later traces neither of the pair appears), while pairs within A21–A25 went from "neither present" in about 85 in 100 traces to co-occurrence in about 82 in 100. Across the two blocks the activities were mutually exclusive in both windows, only with the present side reversed. [REL011, REL013, REL021, REL030, REL038, REL051, REL053, REL056, REL060, REL063, REL015, REL024, REL032, REL039, REL045]
- A29 switched company: earlier it co-occurred with A16–A20 in about 85 in 100 traces (A16 before A29 in about 50, interleaved or repeated in about 35); in the later window it co-occurs with A21–A25 in about 82 in 100 (A21 before A29 in about 47, interleaved or repeated in about 35). [REL020, REL029, REL037, REL044, REL050, REL055, REL059, REL062, REL064, REL065]
- Timing also moved: the elapsed time between A11 and A13 completions roughly doubled (mean about 0.9 to about 1.8 hours, median 0.9 to 1.8), and between A12 and A13 it rose from about 0.16 to about 0.40 hours on average, with more observed intervals (41 to 62). [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]
- Smaller shifts: within the now-dominant branch, A22's outgoing shares became more even (A21 about 58% to 31%, A23 about 29% to 36%, A25 about 13% to 33%; the earlier profile rests on only 31 transitions), and the position gap between A18 and A16/A17 shifted weight between one and two steps (later profiles rest on 17 observations). [DIR002, LAG001, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Main hypothesis: in the later window, the branch executed after A15 was swapped. Traces that previously continued from A15 into the A16–A20 block, together with A29, now continue into the A21–A25 block, which A29 now accompanies; A15's dominant successor changed from A19 to A24. Both branches remain observable at low rates in both windows (about 15–18 in 100 traces each), so this reads as the minority route becoming dominant and the former dominant route becoming minority, not as an activity being added or removed. [OCC001, OCC006, DIR001, REL001, REL006, REL011, REL051, REL055]

The supporting signs are the size and consistency of the participation swap across all ten block activities, the direct redistribution of A15's outgoing transitions from A19 to A24, and the wholesale exchange of co-occurrence and order relations between the two blocks, including A29's switch of company. The screening comparison rules out chance as an explanation of the whole: 79 control-flow items were flagged where about 0.84 would be expected without a change, roughly ninety times that expectation. [DIR001, REL001, REL055, OCC001, OCC006]

Limitations: the evidence shows frequencies and relations, not the routing logic itself. It cannot fully rule out that the two blocks changed through two independent participation adjustments (A16–A20 becoming mostly skipped while A21–A25 became mostly mandatory) rather than a single rerouting at A15, although the redistribution at A15 favours the rerouting reading. [DIR001]

Other differences: the elapsed times on two upstream pairs roughly doubled or more (A11 to A13 about 0.9 to 1.8 hours; A12 to A13 about 0.16 to 0.40 hours, with 41 to 62 observed intervals) — a timing change that stands on its own and that the evidence cannot link to the branch swap; both items far exceed the time-family chance expectation of about 0.006. Within the dominant branch, A22's outgoing shares evened out, but the earlier profile rests on only 31 transitions, and the lag shifts between A18 and A16/A17 rest on 17 later observations, so both are weakly supported. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, DIR002, LAG001, LAG002]
